title: Understanding TDS on Salary: Your Employer's Calculation

faq.q: What is the Income Tax Act 2025?
faq.a: The Income Tax Act 2025 is the new legislation governing income tax in India, effective April 1st, 2026. It replaces the Income Tax Act 1961, updating the legal framework for taxation.

faq.q: Have tax rates changed under the new Act?
faq.a: No, the primary income tax rates and slab structures for individual taxpayers have largely remained unchanged with the introduction of the Income Tax Act 2025. The changes are primarily procedural and administrative.

faq.q: Can my employer deduct more TDS than my actual tax liability?
faq.a: Your employer estimates your annual tax liability based on your declared income and investments. If you haven't declared all your tax-saving investments, they might deduct more. You can claim a refund for any excess TDS when filing your income tax return.

faq.q: What if I switch jobs during the financial year?
faq.a: If you switch jobs, your new employer will calculate TDS based on the income earned from them and any previous income declared by you. It's crucial to provide details of your previous employment's income and TDS to your new employer to avoid under or over-deduction.

faq.q: How does HRA exemption work for TDS calculation?
faq.a: Your employer will exempt the least of the actual HRA received, actual rent paid minus 10% of basic salary, or 40%/50% of basic salary (depending on the city), from your taxable income for TDS purposes.

faq.q: Is professional tax considered for TDS calculation?
faq.a: Yes, any professional tax paid by an employee is deductible from their gross salary before calculating the net taxable income, thereby reducing the overall tax liability.

faq.q: Where can I check the TDS deducted from my salary?
faq.a: You can check the TDS deducted by your employer in your Form 26AS, which is available on the Income Tax India e-filing portal. This form provides a consolidated statement of taxes deducted at source.
